stories.title: China AI developer Z.AI launches $5 billion Hong Kong share, convertible bond sales, term sheet shows
stories.simple_summary: A Chinese AI company is raising $5 billion dollars by selling shares and bonds in Hong Kong. This is a financial deal for investors.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and financial markets — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: The race to build smarter machines ran into a dangerous problem
stories.simple_summary: Developers building AI systems have run into a difficult problem that's slowing down progress. The headline doesn't say exactly what the problem is.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly interesting to tech engineers working on AI — it doesn't affect how you'd use AI in your business right now.

stories.title: Doomsday tech: could AI really kill us all?
stories.simple_summary: This is a headline asking whether AI could become dangerous enough to harm humanity. It's asking a question rather than reporting news.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a big-picture debate that doesn't change anything you'd do today — it's more philosophy than practical news.

stories.title: Readers Write: 9/11, CPR rates, artificial intelligence, immigration
stories.simple_summary: This appears to be a collection of reader letters about various topics including artificial intelligence. No specific AI news story is described.
stories.why_it_matters: Without knowing what the letters say, it's hard to know if this affects you — likely this is just community opinions rather than news you need to know.

stories.title: Jensen Huang explains why Nvidia will grow an astounding 70% next year
stories.simple_summary: Jensen Huang, who runs Nvidia (a company that makes computer chips), says his company will grow very quickly next year because AI companies need lots of chips. This is investor news.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — unless you're buying new computers for your business, you don't need to act on this.

stories.title: Mark Wahlberg is coming to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, and he wants to talk about your work, not his
stories.simple_summary: Actor Mark Wahlberg will speak at a tech conference with Bruce K. Lee about business and investing. This is event news.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly entertainment and conference news — not something that affects your daily life or business.

stories.title: Slack can now vibe-code interactive charts and reports inside chats
stories.simple_summary: Slack (a chat app for teams) is adding a feature where AI can create charts, reports, and dashboards right inside your chats. You'd tell the AI what you need and it would gather the information for you.
stories.why_it_matters: If your small business uses Slack to communicate with your team, this could save you time creating reports and sharing information.

stories.title: OpenAI puts Pro subscriptions on hold due to Astra demand
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI (the company behind ChatGPT) temporarily stopped letting new people buy Pro subscriptions because too many people want it and it's straining their computer systems. They're adding more capacity to handle the demand.
stories.why_it_matters: If you want a Pro subscription, you may have to wait a bit, but the company is working to open it back up soon.

stories.title: Anthropic details distillation campaigns from Alibaba, Moonshot AI, and DeepSeek
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic (an AI company) says that Chinese AI companies have been copying their AI technology without permission and doing it more frequently lately. It's a competition issue.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly a story about AI companies competing and is mostly important to investors and tech industry people.

stories.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse is now the No. 2 app in the US
stories.simple_summary: Meta (which owns Facebook) released a new AI app called Muse that's becoming very popular in the United States, now ranking as the second-most-downloaded app.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Meta products, you might see Muse promoted to you, but whether you use it is entirely optional — nothing you need to do.

stories.title: Schools are catching on to Big Tech’s playbook
stories.simple_summary: AI companies are offering free training and materials to schools to teach students how to use AI. Schools are starting to realize this is how AI companies did the same thing with other technologies in the past.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have kids or grandkids in school, they're likely being taught about AI — this is good, though it's worth knowing that tech companies have an interest in getting people trained on their tools.

stories.title: Anthropic reveals rogue AI agents hate CAPTCHAs, just like you
stories.simple_summary: Researchers found that AI bots trying to act like humans don't like CAPTCHAs (those security puzzles where you prove you're human) just like regular people don't like them.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly interesting to security experts and researchers — it doesn't change anything about your daily AI use.
